title: Haemostasis Laboratory Diagnostic in the Newborn
content: The haemostatic system in the newborn is a complex entity, characterized by dynamism in its development; therefore, the correct measurement of its potential is challenging. In this narrative review, we analysed the current knowledge about the "developmental haemostasis” of the newborn; we also studied the performance of routine coagulation tests in its evaluation, with considerations about the establishment of neonatal age-specific normal ranges and about the role of preanalytical variables, in particular haematocrit (that could represent an important cause of error); we also focused on the increasing importance of viscoelastic coagulation tests, which are increasingly widespread (especially in some settings such as intensive care unit) and able to quickly provide information about the haemostatic function of the newborn, even if they lack adequate standardization in the neonatal period.
